# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +788
- **Deletions**: -133
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T00:45:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1523._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 5 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: error/aborted terminal runs strip the ledger from the persisted transcript but never emit the `task_ledger` record**

This fold only runs on the loop's normal exit. When the run terminates on an error/aborted assistant message, `_terminalRunMessages` (`agent_loop.dart:1221`) emits `AgentEndEvent` and returns early — this call site is never reached. But the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor (`_finalizeGateStrippingSink`) fires for every assistant message DURING the run, so on that path:

- `_persistIncremental` has already appended the **stripped** answer to the session JSONL.
- No `TaskLedgerEvent` is ever emitted → the hidden `task_ledger` record does not exist.
- The early return also ships the **unstripped** original in `AgentEndEvent` (`newMessages` holds the pre-interceptor instance), so the in-memory payload and the persisted JSONL disagree.

Net effect: for a failed/aborted unattended run — precisely the near-miss case the gate exists to capture — the model's self-check is silently discarded. Pre-PR the ledger at least survived in the transcript on this path. This violates the ticket's requirement #2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"): here it parses, is NOT persisted, and the transcript is clean, so the data is unrecoverable.

Suggested fix: run the fold (or at least the stash-matching + `TaskLedgerEvent` emission) before the early return in `_terminalRunMessages`, e.g. pass `strippedLedgers` down and call `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentContext.messages, strippedLedgers, emit)` there too. An aborted run still ends on an assistant answer, so the "run must end on the answer" rule is satisfied. Please also add a test: error/aborted stopReason + parseable terminal ledger ⇒ record persists and transcript stays clean.

---

### Thread 8 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "mid-run flip" rationale describes a scenario that cannot happen**

The comment says the gate key "reads the LIVE config so a mid-run flip stays consistent between the two halves" — but nothing in the loop can flip `finalizeGate` mid-run: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces `model` (`AgentLoopConfig.copyWith({Model? model})` carries `finalizeGate` through unchanged), and a host mutating `Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. Within a run the value is constant, so the live-read buys nothing and the comment promises a knob that doesn't exist — a future reader may assume an interactive toggle is honored here. Consider trimming the sentence to state the simpler truth (the key is read per event so the interceptor and the fold always agree on the same config instance), or dropping the closure in favor of capturing the bool directly.

---

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the unfenced shape can strip a legitimate "documentation" answer**

The unfenced near-miss detector keys on a bare `task-ledger` heading followed by `- requirement: …` bullets — but that is also exactly what a model answering "what does the task-ledger look like?" (or documenting the format) would emit, e.g.:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

That parses as a one-item ledger and `_stripAssistantLedger` removes the whole section from the final answer of an unattended run, mangling a correct response. The fenced shape doesn't have this problem (models only fence it when actually producing the contract artifact). Consider tightening the unfenced acceptance — e.g. require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field, or two-plus entries — so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger. Low probability, but the strip is silent and user-facing.

---

### Thread 10 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`

# pr-1523: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1523
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1523
- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +788
- **Deletions**: -133
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T00:45:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1523._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 5 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: error/aborted terminal runs strip the ledger from the persisted transcript but never emit the `task_ledger` record**

This fold only runs on the loop's normal exit. When the run terminates on an error/aborted assistant message, `_terminalRunMessages` (`agent_loop.dart:1221`) emits `AgentEndEvent` and returns early — this call site is never reached. But the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor (`_finalizeGateStrippingSink`) fires for every assistant message DURING the run, so on that path:

- `_persistIncremental` has already appended the **stripped** answer to the session JSONL.
- No `TaskLedgerEvent` is ever emitted → the hidden `task_ledger` record does not exist.
- The early return also ships the **unstripped** original in `AgentEndEvent` (`newMessages` holds the pre-interceptor instance), so the in-memory payload and the persisted JSONL disagree.

Net effect: for a failed/aborted unattended run — precisely the near-miss case the gate exists to capture — the model's self-check is silently discarded. Pre-PR the ledger at least survived in the transcript on this path. This violates the ticket's requirement #2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"): here it parses, is NOT persisted, and the transcript is clean, so the data is unrecoverable.

Suggested fix: run the fold (or at least the stash-matching + `TaskLedgerEvent` emission) before the early return in `_terminalRunMessages`, e.g. pass `strippedLedgers` down and call `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentContext.messages, strippedLedgers, emit)` there too. An aborted run still ends on an assistant answer, so the "run must end on the answer" rule is satisfied. Please also add a test: error/aborted stopReason + parseable terminal ledger ⇒ record persists and transcript stays clean.

---

### Thread 8 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "mid-run flip" rationale describes a scenario that cannot happen**

The comment says the gate key "reads the LIVE config so a mid-run flip stays consistent between the two halves" — but nothing in the loop can flip `finalizeGate` mid-run: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces `model` (`AgentLoopConfig.copyWith({Model? model})` carries `finalizeGate` through unchanged), and a host mutating `Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. Within a run the value is constant, so the live-read buys nothing and the comment promises a knob that doesn't exist — a future reader may assume an interactive toggle is honored here. Consider trimming the sentence to state the simpler truth (the key is read per event so the interceptor and the fold always agree on the same config instance), or dropping the closure in favor of capturing the bool directly.

---

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the unfenced shape can strip a legitimate "documentation" answer**

The unfenced near-miss detector keys on a bare `task-ledger` heading followed by `- requirement: …` bullets — but that is also exactly what a model answering "what does the task-ledger look like?" (or documenting the format) would emit, e.g.:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

That parses as a one-item ledger and `_stripAssistantLedger` removes the whole section from the final answer of an unattended run, mangling a correct response. The fenced shape doesn't have this problem (models only fence it when actually producing the contract artifact). Consider tightening the unfenced acceptance — e.g. require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field, or two-plus entries — so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger. Low probability, but the strip is silent and user-facing.

---

### Thread 10 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: only one text block is stripped per message — a second ledger-bearing block stays in the transcript**

`_stripAssistantLedger` resolves blocks last-to-first and returns after replacing the FIRST ledger-bearing block. If a message ever carries two text blocks that each parse as a ledger (e.g. a revised answer plus the original), the earlier block is left in the stripped message and renders in the transcript — while the doc-level contract says "the transcript never shows it". This matches the old gate's last-block-keyed semantics (so event behavior is consistent), but the strip guarantee is per-message-one-block. In practice models emit a single text block, so impact is negligible; if you want the guarantee to hold, loop over all blocks and replace every ledger-bearing one (recording one stash entry per block, or the last).

---

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The attendance re-keying (`headlessRun` instead of `approvalMode`) is the right fix for the interactive-autopilot regression, and the tolerant unfenced-ledger parsing is well tested — but the ledger strip lands too late: the final message is streamed to stdout and persisted to the session JSONL before the fold runs, so the persisted transcript (resume, `fa trajectory`, bench log sync) still shows the ledger the ticket says must never render. One ticket-requirement gap (no concrete negative examples in the prompt) and four smaller polish items below.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 The fold runs after `MessageEndEvent` — persistence and live render already happened (comment1)
- ⚠️ Ticket req #1 asked for 2-3 concrete negative examples in the prompt; only an abstract rule was added (comment2)

**Next Steps**:
1. Make the strip effective for the persisted/streamed transcript, not just the in-memory/event payload (see comment1 for options)
2. Add the concrete "why did you…" / "what does X do…" negative examples to `finalize_gate.md`
3. Address the suggestion-level items as time permits — none block merge

# pr-1523: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix

- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1523
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1523
- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +788
- **Deletions**: -133
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T00:45:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1523._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 5 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: error/aborted terminal runs strip the ledger from the persisted transcript but never emit the `task_ledger` record**

This fold only runs on the loop's normal exit. When the run terminates on an error/aborted assistant message, `_terminalRunMessages` (`agent_loop.dart:1221`) emits `AgentEndEvent` and returns early — this call site is never reached. But the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor (`_finalizeGateStrippingSink`) fires for every assistant message DURING the run, so on that path:

- `_persistIncremental` has already appended the **stripped** answer to the session JSONL.
- No `TaskLedgerEvent` is ever emitted → the hidden `task_ledger` record does not exist.
- The early return also ships the **unstripped** original in `AgentEndEvent` (`newMessages` holds the pre-interceptor instance), so the in-memory payload and the persisted JSONL disagree.

Net effect: for a failed/aborted unattended run — precisely the near-miss case the gate exists to capture — the model's self-check is silently discarded. Pre-PR the ledger at least survived in the transcript on this path. This violates the ticket's requirement #2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"): here it parses, is NOT persisted, and the transcript is clean, so the data is unrecoverable.

Suggested fix: run the fold (or at least the stash-matching + `TaskLedgerEvent` emission) before the early return in `_terminalRunMessages`, e.g. pass `strippedLedgers` down and call `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentContext.messages, strippedLedgers, emit)` there too. An aborted run still ends on an assistant answer, so the "run must end on the answer" rule is satisfied. Please also add a test: error/aborted stopReason + parseable terminal ledger ⇒ record persists and transcript stays clean.

---

### Thread 8 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "mid-run flip" rationale describes a scenario that cannot happen**

The comment says the gate key "reads the LIVE config so a mid-run flip stays consistent between the two halves" — but nothing in the loop can flip `finalizeGate` mid-run: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces `model` (`AgentLoopConfig.copyWith({Model? model})` carries `finalizeGate` through unchanged), and a host mutating `Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. Within a run the value is constant, so the live-read buys nothing and the comment promises a knob that doesn't exist — a future reader may assume an interactive toggle is honored here. Consider trimming the sentence to state the simpler truth (the key is read per event so the interceptor and the fold always agree on the same config instance), or dropping the closure in favor of capturing the bool directly.

---

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the unfenced shape can strip a legitimate "documentation" answer**

# pr-1523: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be

contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.

  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.

    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1523._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: error/aborted terminal runs strip the ledger from the persisted transcript but never emit the `task_ledger` record**

This fold only runs on the loop's normal exit. When the run terminates on an error/aborted assistant message, `_terminalRunMessages` (`agent_loop.dart:1221`) emits `AgentEndEvent` and returns early — this call site is never reached. But the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor (`_finalizeGateStrippingSink`) fires for every assistant message DURING the run, so on that path:

- `_persistIncremental` has already appended the **stripped** answer to the session JSONL.
- No `TaskLedgerEvent` is ever emitted → the hidden `task_ledger` record does not exist.
- The early return also ships the **unstripped** original in `AgentEndEvent` (`newMessages` holds the pre-interceptor instance), so the in-memory payload and the persisted JSONL disagree.

Net effect: for a failed/aborted unattended run — precisely the near-miss case the gate exists to capture — the model's self-check is silently discarded. Pre-PR the ledger at least survived in the transcript on this path. This violates the ticket's requirement #2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"): here it parses, is NOT persisted, and the transcript is clean, so the data is unrecoverable.

Suggested fix: run the fold (or at least the stash-matching + `TaskLedgerEvent` emission) before the early return in `_terminalRunMessages`, e.g. pass `strippedLedgers` down and call `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentContext.messages, strippedLedgers, emit)` there too. An aborted run still ends on an assistant answer, so the "run must end on the answer" rule is satisfied. Please also add a test: error/aborted stopReason + parseable terminal ledger ⇒ record persists and transcript stays clean.

---

### Thread 8 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "mid-run flip" rationale describes a scenario that cannot happen**

The comment says the gate key "reads the LIVE config so a mid-run flip stays consistent between the two halves" — but nothing in the loop can flip `finalizeGate` mid-run: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces `model` (`AgentLoopConfig.copyWith({Model? model})` carries `finalizeGate` through unchanged), and a host mutating `Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. Within a run the value is constant, so the live-read buys nothing and the comment promises a knob that doesn't exist — a future reader may assume an interactive toggle is honored here. Consider trimming the sentence to state the simpler truth (the key is read per event so the interceptor and the fold always agree on the same config instance), or dropping the closure in favor of capturing the bool directly.

---

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the unfenced shape can strip a legitimate "documentation" answer**

The unfenced near-miss detector keys on a bare `task-ledger` heading followed by `- requirement: …` bullets — but that is also exactly what a model answering "what does the task-ledger look like?" (or documenting the format) would emit, e.g.:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

That parses as a one-item ledger and `_stripAssistantLedger` removes the whole section from the final answer of an unattended run, mangling a correct response. The fenced shape doesn't have this problem (models only fence it when actually producing the contract artifact). Consider tightening the unfenced acceptance — e.g. require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field, or two-plus entries — so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger. Low probability, but the strip is silent and user-facing.

---

### Thread 10 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: only one text block is stripped per message — a second ledger-bearing block stays in the transcript**

`_stripAssistantLedger` resolves blocks last-to-first and returns after replacing the FIRST ledger-bearing block. If a message ever carries two text blocks that each parse as a ledger (e.g. a revised answer plus the original), the earlier block is left in the stripped message and renders in the transcript — while the doc-level contract says "the transcript never shows it". This matches the old gate's last-block-keyed semantics (so event behavior is consistent), but the strip guarantee is per-message-one-block. In practice models emit a single text block, so impact is negligible; if you want the guarantee to hold, loop over all blocks and replace every ledger-bearing one (recording one stash entry per block, or the last).

---

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The attendance re-keying (`headlessRun` instead of `approvalMode`) is the right fix for the interactive-autopilot regression, and the tolerant unfenced-ledger parsing is well tested — but the ledger strip lands too late: the final message is streamed to stdout and persisted to the session JSONL before the fold runs, so the persisted transcript (resume, `fa trajectory`, bench log sync) still shows the ledger the ticket says must never render. **Next Steps**:
1. Make the strip effective for the persisted/streamed transcript, not just the in-memory/event payload (see comment1 for options)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1523._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 5 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: error/aborted terminal runs strip the ledger from the persisted transcript but never emit the `task_ledger` record**

This fold only runs on the loop's normal exit. When the run terminates on an error/aborted assistant message, `_terminalRunMessages` (`agent_loop.dart:1221`) emits `AgentEndEvent` and returns early — this call site is never reached. But the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor (`_finalizeGateStrippingSink`) fires for every assistant message DURING the run, so on that path:

- `_persistIncremental` has already appended the **stripped** answer to the session JSONL.
- No `TaskLedgerEvent` is ever emitted → the hidden `task_ledger` record does not exist.
- The early return also ships the **unstripped** original in `AgentEndEvent` (`newMessages` holds the pre-interceptor instance), so the in-memory payload and the persisted JSONL disagree.

Net effect: for a failed/aborted unattended run — precisely the near-miss case the gate exists to capture — the model's self-check is silently discarded. Pre-PR the ledger at least survived in the transcript on this path. This violates the ticket's requirement #2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"): here it parses, is NOT persisted, and the transcript is clean, so the data is unrecoverable.

Suggested fix: run the fold (or at least the stash-matching + `TaskLedgerEvent` emission) before the early return in `_terminalRunMessages`, e.g. pass `strippedLedgers` down and call `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentContext.messages, strippedLedgers, emit)` there too. An aborted run still ends on an assistant answer, so the "run must end on the answer" rule is satisfied. Please also add a test: error/aborted stopReason + parseable terminal ledger ⇒ record persists and transcript stays clean.

---

### Thread 8 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "mid-run flip" rationale describes a scenario that cannot happen**

The comment says the gate key "reads the LIVE config so a mid-run flip stays consistent between the two halves" — but nothing in the loop can flip `finalizeGate` mid-run: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces `model` (`AgentLoopConfig.copyWith({Model? model})` carries `finalizeGate` through unchanged), and a host mutating `Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. Within a run the value is constant, so the live-read buys nothing and the comment promises a knob that doesn't exist — a future reader may assume an interactive toggle is honored here. Consider trimming the sentence to state the simpler truth (the key is read per event so the interceptor and the fold always agree on the same config instance), or dropping the closure in favor of capturing the bool directly.

---

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the unfenced shape can strip a legitimate "documentation" answer**

The unfenced near-miss detector keys on a bare `task-ledger` heading followed by `- requirement: …` bullets — but that is also exactly what a model answering "what does the task-ledger look like?" (or documenting the format) would emit, e.g.:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

That parses as a one-item ledger and `_stripAssistantLedger` removes the whole section from the final answer of an unattended run, mangling a correct response. The fenced shape doesn't have this problem (models only fence it when actually producing the contract artifact). Consider tightening the unfenced acceptance — e.g. require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field, or two-plus entries — so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger. Low probability, but the strip is silent and user-facing.

---

### Thread 10 — `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: only one text block is stripped per message — a second ledger-bearing block stays in the transcript**

`_stripAssistantLedger` resolves blocks last-to-first and returns after replacing the FIRST ledger-bearing block. If a message ever carries two text blocks that each parse as a ledger (e.g. a revised answer plus the original), the earlier block is left in the stripped message and renders in the transcript — while the doc-level contract says "the transcript never shows it". This matches the old gate's last-block-keyed semantics (so event behavior is consistent), but the strip guarantee is per-message-one-block. In practice models emit a single text block, so impact is negligible; if you want the guarantee to hold, loop over all blocks and replace every ledger-bearing one (recording one stash entry per block, or the last).

---

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# pr-1523: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.
