## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {

  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).

Now decide the rule. The reviewer's example doc:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,

The documenting test still parses. Why? The doc example:

```
The contract asks for a checklist like this:

## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail

Each entry quotes the requirement verbatim.
```

`_parseLedgerItems` on body:
- `- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>` → entry, requirement = '<verbatim requirement quote>'
- `  status: pass|fixed|fail` → field line, status = 'pass|fixed|fail' → fromName → token 'pass|fixed|fail'.split(whitespace).first = 'pass|fixed|fail', startsWith('pass') → TaskLedgerItemStatus.pass!

So `only.status != fail` → true → looks like a ledger. The placeholder "pass|fixed|fail" parses as pass. Hmm.

The reviewer said: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field". A "real" status field means a status value that's actually one of the enum values, not the literal placeholder. So I should distinguish "status field present with a recognized value" — fromName is tolerant though. Better: check whether the item's status field actually parses to a recognized token. Options:

1. Check the raw body for a status field with a clean token. But `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` receives items only.

2. Change the acceptance rule: for a single entry, require non-empty command/expected/actual OR status recognized — where "recognized" means the status token (trimmed) is exactly 'pass', 'fixed', or 'fail' (case-insensitive) or starts with them? But 'pass|fixed|fail' starts with 'pass'...

Hmm. The doc example's status is 'pass|fixed|fail'. What distinguishes a real near-miss single entry from this doc? Honestly the cleanest discriminator per the reviewer: "two-plus entries". The reviewer's first alternative: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field" — a "real" field = a field that carries actual verification content. `command: test -f script.py` is real; `status: pass|fixed|fail` is a placeholder enumeration.

Practical approach: for a single entry, require `command`/`expected`/`actual` non-empty, OR a status token that is exactly an outcome word (matches `^(pass|fixed|fail)\b` as a whole word without trailing junk? 'pass|fixed|fail' — word boundary: 'pass' followed by '|' — `\b` between 's' and '|' is a boundary (word char → non-word char). So `pass|fixed|fail` matches `^pass\b`. Hmm.

Alternative: require the status value to be EXACTLY one of pass/fixed/fail (case-insensitive, maybe with checkmark suffix). 'PASS ✅' is a legit tolerant token in the fenced tests. But for the unfenced near-miss, do we need that tolerance? The tolerance was added for the fenced contract shape mostly.

Simpler and defensible: single unfenced entry is accepted only if it has a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field — actual verification evidence. blocks.text:
Only the fenced shape is used in the CLI/integration tests; the unfenced shape appears in `finalize_gate_test.dart` and `finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` only. Both of those unfenced fixtures carry `command:` (and status pass).

Now decide the rule. The reviewer's example doc:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

Only the fenced shape appears in CLI/integration tests, so tightening is safe. The discriminator: a `status` claim alone is exactly what a format quote carries — real verification evidence is a `command`/`expected`/`actual` field. Updating the rule:

Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

Only the fenced shape appears in CLI/integration tests, so tightening is safe. The discriminator: a `status` claim alone is exactly what a format quote carries — real verification evidence is a `command`/`expected`/`actual` field. Updating the rule:

messages.preview: The placeholder `status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`. Let me check all unfenced-shape usages in tests before adjusting the rule:

blocks.text:
The documenting test still parses. Why? The doc example:

```
The contract asks for a checklist like this:

## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail

Each entry quotes the requirement verbatim.
```

`_parseLedgerItems` on body:
- `- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>` → entry, requirement = '<verbatim requirement quote>'
- `  status: pass|fixed|fail` → field line, status = 'pass|fixed|fail' → fromName → token 'pass|fixed|fail'.split(whitespace).first = 'pass|fixed|fail', startsWith('pass') → TaskLedgerItemStatus.pass!

So `only.status != fail` → true → looks like a ledger. The placeholder "pass|fixed|fail" parses as pass. Hmm.

The reviewer said: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field". A "real" status field means a status value that's actually one of the enum values, not the literal placeholder. So I should distinguish "status field present with a recognized value" — fromName is tolerant though. Better: check whether the item's status field actually parses to a recognized token. Options:

1. Check the raw body for a status field with a clean token. But `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` receives items only.

2. Change the acceptance rule: for a single entry, require non-empty command/expected/actual OR status recognized — where "recognized" means the status token (trimmed) is exactly 'pass', 'fixed', or 'fail' (case-insensitive) or starts with them? But 'pass|fixed|fail' starts with 'pass'...

Hmm. The doc example's status is 'pass|fixed|fail'. What distinguishes a real near-miss single entry from this doc? Honestly the cleanest discriminator per the reviewer: "two-plus entries". The reviewer's first alternative: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field" — a "real" field = a field that carries actual verification content. `command: test -f script.py` is real; `status: pass|fixed|fail` is a placeholder enumeration.

Practical approach: for a single entry, require `command`/`expected`/`actual` non-empty, OR a status token that is exactly an outcome word (matches `^(pass|fixed|fail)\b` as a whole word without trailing junk? 'pass|fixed|fail' — word boundary: 'pass' followed by '|' — `\b` between 's' and '|' is a boundary (word char → non-word char). So `pass|fixed|fail` matches `^pass\b`. Hmm.

Alternative: require the status value to be EXACTLY one of pass/fixed/fail (case-insensitive, maybe with checkmark suffix). 'PASS ✅' is a legit tolerant token in the fenced tests. But for the unfenced near-miss, do we need that tolerance? The tolerance was added for the fenced contract shape mostly.

Simpler and defensible: single unfenced entry is accepted only if it has a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field — actual verification evidence. A status alone is just a claim; the verification command/expectation/actual is what separates a ledger from a format doc. But the loop test's unfenced near-miss: has command. The bold heading test: has command. The prompt-test fixtures? Let me check what other tests use the unfenced shape — the prompt test and integration test. blocks.text:
Only the fenced shape is used in the CLI/integration tests; the unfenced shape appears in `finalize_gate_test.dart` and `finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` only. Both of those unfenced fixtures carry `command:` (and status pass).

Now decide the rule. The reviewer's example doc:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

Only the fenced shape appears in CLI/integration tests, so tightening is safe. The discriminator: a `status` claim alone is exactly what a format quote carries — real verification evidence is a `command`/`expected`/`actual` field. Updating the rule:

bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {

  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}

messages.preview: The placeholder `status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`. Let me check all unfenced-shape usages in tests before adjusting the rule:

blocks.text:
The documenting test still parses. Why? The doc example:

```
The contract asks for a checklist like this:

## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail

Each entry quotes the requirement verbatim.
```

`_parseLedgerItems` on body:
- `- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>` → entry, requirement = '<verbatim requirement quote>'
- `  status: pass|fixed|fail` → field line, status = 'pass|fixed|fail' → fromName → token 'pass|fixed|fail'.split(whitespace).first = 'pass|fixed|fail', startsWith('pass') → TaskLedgerItemStatus.pass!

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}

messages.preview: The placeholder `status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`. Let me check all unfenced-shape usages in tests before adjusting the rule:

blocks.text:
The documenting test still parses. Why? The doc example:

```
The contract asks for a checklist like this:

## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail

Each entry quotes the requirement verbatim.
```

`_parseLedgerItems` on body:
- `- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>` → entry, requirement = '<verbatim requirement quote>'
- `  status: pass|fixed|fail` → field line, status = 'pass|fixed|fail' → fromName → token 'pass|fixed|fail'.split(whitespace).first = 'pass|fixed|fail', startsWith('pass') → TaskLedgerItemStatus.pass!

So `only.status != fail` → true → looks like a ledger. The placeholder "pass|fixed|fail" parses as pass. Hmm.

The reviewer said: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field". A "real" status field means a status value that's actually one of the enum values, not the literal placeholder. So I should distinguish "status field present with a recognized value" — fromName is tolerant though. Better: check whether the item's status field actually parses to a recognized token. Options:

1. Check the raw body for a status field with a clean token. But `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` receives items only.

2. Change the acceptance rule: for a single entry, require non-empty command/expected/actual OR status recognized — where "recognized" means the status token (trimmed) is exactly 'pass', 'fixed', or 'fail' (case-insensitive) or starts with them? But 'pass|fixed|fail' starts with 'pass'...

Hmm. The doc example's status is 'pass|fixed|fail'. What distinguishes a real near-miss single entry from this doc? Honestly the cleanest discriminator per the reviewer: "two-plus entries". The reviewer's first alternative: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field" — a "real" field = a field that carries actual verification content. `command: test -f script.py` is real; `status: pass|fixed|fail` is a placeholder enumeration.

Practical approach: for a single entry, require `command`/`expected`/`actual` non-empty, OR a status token that is exactly an outcome word (matches `^(pass|fixed|fail)\b` as a whole word without trailing junk? 'pass|fixed|fail' — word boundary: 'pass' followed by '|' — `\b` between 's' and '|' is a boundary (word char → non-word char). So `pass|fixed|fail` matches `^pass\b`. Hmm.

Alternative: require the status value to be EXACTLY one of pass/fixed/fail (case-insensitive, maybe with checkmark suffix). 'PASS ✅' is a legit tolerant token in the fenced tests. But for the unfenced near-miss, do we need that tolerance? The tolerance was added for the fenced contract shape mostly.

Simpler and defensible: single unfenced entry is accepted only if it has a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field — actual verification evidence. A status alone is just a claim; the verification command/expectation/actual is what separates a ledger from a format doc. But the loop test's unfenced near-miss: has command. Only the fenced shape is used in the CLI/integration tests; the unfenced shape appears in `finalize_gate_test.dart` and `finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` only. Both of those unfenced fixtures carry `command:` (and status pass).

Now decide the rule. The reviewer's example doc:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

Only the fenced shape appears in CLI/integration tests, so tightening is safe. The discriminator: a `status` claim alone is exactly what a format quote carries — real verification evidence is a `command`/`expected`/`actual` field. Updating the rule:

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

# Fixed — the terminal fold now runs on the error/aborted early-return path

`_terminalRunMessages` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`) now receives the strip
stash, the context messages, and the gate flag, and runs
`_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentMessages, strippedLedgers, emit)`
**before** emitting `TurnEndEvent`/`AgentEndEvent` and returning early:

```dart
if (finalizeGate) {
  await _emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, contextMessages, stash, emit);
}
await emit(TurnEndEvent(message: message, toolResults: const []));
await emit(AgentEndEvent(List.unmodifiable(newMessages)));
```

Effects on the failed/aborted path:

- The hidden `task_ledger` record **persists** — the self-check of exactly the
  near-miss case the gate exists to capture is no longer discarded.
- `AgentEndEvent` now ships the **stripped** terminal message (the fold
  rewrites `newMessages` before the snapshot is taken), so the in-memory
  payload and the persisted JSONL agree.
- gh-1412's "run must end on the answer" is preserved: the fold still only
  fires when the terminal assistant message's original is in the stash.

Regression test per your requirement in
`test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`: *"an error/aborted terminal answer
still folds — the hidden record persists and the end payload ships the
stripped message"* — `stopReason: error` + a tool turn + parseable terminal
ledger ⇒ exactly one `TaskLedgerEvent`, and the `AgentEndEvent` payload
contains no `task-ledger`/fence. RED before the fix (zero events), green
after; the surrounding finalize-gate suites stay green.

# Fixed — comment now states the constant truth

The comment in `_runAgentLoop` no longer promises a mid-run flip that cannot
happen. It now reads:

> The gate key is read per event from the loop's live config so the
> interceptor and the fold always agree on the same value; within a run it
> is constant — nothing in the loop mutates `finalizeGate` mid-run.

That matches the mechanics you traced: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces
`model` (`copyWith` carries `finalizeGate` through), and a host mutating
`Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. The
closure stays (the fold and the interceptor must read the same config
instance per event), but the text no longer implies an honored interactive
toggle.

# Fixed — the unfenced shape now requires real verification evidence

New `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` gate in `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`
(consulted from `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` for unfenced spans only; the
fenced contract shape is untouched):

- **two-plus entries** → accepted (a real near-miss checklist);
- **a single entry** → accepted only when it carries actual verification
  content: a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field;
- otherwise the span is skipped — a prose section quoting the format is never
  classified as a ledger.

A `status` claim alone is deliberately not evidence: your doc example's
`status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check
would not have closed the window — but it never carries a
command/expectation/actual, so it is rejected now. A lone
`- requirement:` bullet in particular is never enough.

Regression tests in `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart`:

- *"a model DOCUMENTING the ledger format is not stripped"* — your exact
  heading + single-bullet + `status: pass|fixed|fail` example ⇒
  `parseTaskLedger` null and `stripTaskLedger` byte-identical. RED before
  the fix (parsed as a one-item ledger).
- *"a single-entry near-miss with a real command still parses"* — positive
  control so the tightening doesn't lose genuine one-item self-checks.

All pre-existing unfenced fixtures (two-item near-miss, bold heading, loop
test) carry real commands and stay green.

# Fixed — every ledger-bearing block is stripped; the gate key stays last-block

`_stripAssistantLedger` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`) no
longer returns after the first ledger-bearing block. It now walks all text
blocks last-to-first, replaces **every** ledger-bearing one, and records ONE
stash entry per message:

- the stash entry's `stripped` message has all ledger blocks removed, so the
  persisted JSONL and the rendered transcript can never show a leftover
  block ("the transcript never shows it" now holds per message, not per
  first-hit);
- the stash entry's `ledger` stays the **last** ledger-bearing block's
  resolution (`ledger ??= ...` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412's
  "last block decides" event semantics are unchanged, so the gate key and
  the fold's stash-matching behave exactly as before;
- one stash entry per message keeps the fold's `identical(entry.original,
  terminal)` matching untouched.

Regression test in `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`: *"EVERY
ledger-bearing text block is stripped — a second block never survives in the
transcript (the gate key stays the last ledger)"* — a message with two text
blocks that each carry a fenced ledger ⇒ both blocks gone from the
`AgentEndEvent` payload, and the single `TaskLedgerEvent` carries the LAST
block's ledger (`revised item`). RED before the fix (the draft block
survived), green after.

bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {

{"content":"# Fixed — the terminal fold now runs on the error/aborted early-return path

`_terminalRunMessages` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`) now receives the strip

`_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentMessages, strippedLedgers, emit)`
**before** emitting `TurnEndEvent`/`AgentEndEvent` and returning early:

```dart
if (finalizeGate) {
  await _emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, contextMessages, stash, emit);
}
await emit(TurnEndEvent(message: message, toolResults: const []));
await emit(AgentEndEvent(List.unmodifiable(newMessages)));
```

Effects on the failed/aborted path:

- The hidden `task_ledger` record **persists** — the self-check of exactly the
  near-miss case the gate exists to capture is no longer discarded.
- `AgentEndEvent` now ships the **stripped** terminal message (the fold
  rewrites `newMessages` before the snapshot is taken), so the in-memory
  payload and the persisted JSONL agree.
- gh-1412's "run must end on the answer" is preserved: the fold still only
  fires when the terminal assistant message's original is in the stash.

Regression test per your requirement in
`test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`: *"an error/aborted terminal answer
still folds — the hidden record persists and the end payload ships the
stripped message"* — `stopReason: error` + a tool turn + parseable terminal
ledger ⇒ exactly one `TaskLedgerEvent`, and the `AgentEndEvent` payload

","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_7_terminal_fold.md"}

{"content":"# Fixed — comment now states the constant truth

The comment in `_runAgentLoop` no longer promises a mid-run flip that cannot
happen. It now reads:

> The gate key is read per event from the loop's live config so the
> interceptor and the fold always agree on the same value; within a run it
> is constant — nothing in the loop mutates `finalizeGate` mid-run.

That matches the mechanics you traced: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces
`model` (`copyWith` carries `finalizeGate` through), and a host mutating
`Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. The
closure stays (the fold and the interceptor must read the same config
instance per event), but the text no longer implies an honored interactive
toggle.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_8_comment.md"}

{"content":"# Fixed — the unfenced shape now requires real verification evidence

New `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` gate in `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`
(consulted from `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` for unfenced spans only; the
fenced contract shape is untouched):

- **two-plus entries** → accepted (a real near-miss checklist);
- **a single entry** → accepted only when it carries actual verification
  content: a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field;
- otherwise the span is skipped — a prose section quoting the format is never
  classified as a ledger.

A `status` claim alone is deliberately not evidence: your doc example's
`status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check
would not have closed the window — but it never carries a
command/expectation/actual, so it is rejected now. A lone
`- requirement:` bullet in particular is never enough.

longer returns after the first ledger-bearing block. It now walks all text

- the stash entry's `ledger` stays the **last** ledger-bearing block's
  resolution (`ledger ??= ...` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412's

  the fold's stash-matching behave exactly as before;
- one stash entry per message keeps the fold's `identical(entry.original,
  terminal)` matching untouched.

bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {

  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}

{"content":"# Fixed — the unfenced shape now requires real verification evidence

New `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` gate in `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`
(consulted from `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` for unfenced spans only; the
fenced contract shape is untouched):

- **two-plus entries** → accepted (a real near-miss checklist);
- **a single entry** → accepted only when it carries actual verification

# 🔧 Rework Complete — gh-1516

All four open review threads on head `6bff6972b` addressed in code, each with a
RED-before/GREEN-after regression test. No open threads were skipped.

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 7 (IMPORTANT)** — error/aborted terminal runs stripped the ledger from
  the persisted JSONL (the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor fires during the run)
  but never emitted the `task_ledger` record: `_terminalRunMessages` returned
  early, bypassing `_emitFinalizeGateFold`. The self-check of a failed
  unattended run — precisely the near-miss the gate exists to capture — was
  silently discarded, and `AgentEndEvent` shipped the unstripped original,
  disagreeing with the persisted session.
- **Thread 8** — the gate-key comment promised a "mid-run flip" that nothing in
  the loop can perform; the promise of a nonexistent knob could mislead future
  readers.
- **Thread 9** — the unfenced near-miss detector keyed on a bare `task-ledger`
  heading + `- requirement:` bullets, which is also exactly what a model
  *documenting the format* emits; the silent strip could mangle a correct
  answer. Note the review's example (`status: pass|fixed|fail`) parses
  tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check alone would not close the
  window — the fix requires real verification content instead.
- **Thread 10** — `_stripAssistantLedger` returned after the first
  ledger-bearing block, so a second ledger-bearing text block stayed in the
  transcript, violating the per-message "transcript never shows it" guarantee.
- **Machine-notice threads** (verdict records + `rework-consume` audits,
  `threadId: null`) are audit boilerplate whose own text says "Do not edit or
  reply" — no reply targets. The two review-summary comments (REQUEST_CHANGES
  round + APPROVE round) are answered by this response: the APPROVE leg's one
  remaining IMPORTANT issue is thread 7, fixed below; its three polish items
  are threads 8/9/10, also fixed.

## Approach

TDD per thread — a failing test reproducing the exact scenario first, then the
minimum fix:

1. **Terminal fold (thread 7)** — `_terminalRunMessages` now takes the context
   messages, the strip stash, and the gate flag, and runs
   `_emitFinalizeGateFold` before the early return. Effects: the hidden
   `task_ledger` record persists on error/aborted runs; `AgentEndEvent` ships
   the stripped terminal message (fold rewrites `newMessages` before the
   snapshot), so the in-memory payload and the session JSONL agree; gh-1412's
   "run must end on the answer" is untouched (the fold still only fires when
   the terminal message's original is in the stash).
2. **Comment truth (thread 8)** — the gate-key comment now states that the key
   is read per event from the live config so interceptor and fold agree, and
   that within a run the value is constant because nothing mutates
   `finalizeGate` mid-run. The closure stays (both halves must read the same
   config instance).
3. **Unfenced evidence bar (thread 9)** — new `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` in
   `finalize_gate.dart`, consulted for unfenced spans only (fenced contract
   shape unchanged): two-plus entries, OR a single entry with a non-empty
   `command`/`expected`/`actual`. A lone `- requirement:` bullet — or a status
   placeholder — never classifies a prose section as a ledger.
4. **Per-message strip (thread 10)** — `_stripAssistantLedger` now walks all
   text blocks and replaces every ledger-bearing one, recording ONE stash
   entry per message whose `ledger` stays the LAST block's resolution
   (`ledger ??=` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412 "last block decides"
   event semantics preserved, fold stash-matching untouched.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `_terminalRunMessages` signature +
  pre-return fold; gate-key comment rewritten (thread 7 + 8).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart` — `_stripAssistantLedger`
  strips all ledger-bearing blocks, one stash entry per message (thread 10).
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — `_LedgerSpan.isUnfenced` +
  `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` evidence gate in `_lastParseableLedgerSpan`
  (thread 9).
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — RED→GREEN: error-stopReason
  terminal fold test; two-block strip test; `textTurn`/`assistant` gained a
  `stopReason` parameter.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — RED→GREEN: documenting-the-format
  rejected (parse null, strip byte-identical); single-entry-with-command
  positive control.

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproduced first**: all three new tests failed on the pre-fix head —
  zero `TaskLedgerEvent` on the error path; the draft ledger block survived
  the strip; the format-documentation answer parsed as a ledger.
- **GREEN after the fix**: finalize-gate suites all pass —
  `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart`, `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart` (50 tests), plus
  `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration` (2/2).
- **Full suite** (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,llm,pty,browser-ext,io,perf`):
  see final count below — no regressions.
- `dart analyze lib/src/cli lib/src/agent test/agent test/cli`: no
  errors/warnings (only pre-existing info-level `unnecessary_import` notices
  in untouched files).
- `dart format` clean on all touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- **CRAP ratchet** (CI's exact tool, `crap4dart 0.11.0`): `analyze` —
  `_terminalRunMessages` CC 4, `_stripAssistantLedger` CC 6,
  `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` CC 5, `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` CC 4,
  `_runAgentLoop` CC 9; Max CRAP 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00).
  `check --baseline`: 3 passed, 1 warned (the pre-existing warning-severity
  duplication triage debt — unchanged from the previous round).

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

{"content":"# 🔧 Rework Complete — gh-1516

All four open review threads on head `6bff6972b` addressed in code, each with a
RED-before/GREEN-after regression test. No open threads were skipped.

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 7 (IMPORTANT)** — error/aborted terminal runs stripped the ledger from
  the persisted JSONL (the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor fires during the run)
  but never emitted the `task_ledger` record: `_terminalRunMessages` returned
  early, bypassing `_emitFinalizeGateFold`. The self-check of a failed
  unattended run — precisely the near-miss the gate exists to capture — was
  silently discarded, and `AgentEndEvent` shipped the unstripped original,
  disagreeing with the persisted session.
- **Thread 8** — the gate-key comment promised a "mid-run flip" that nothing in
  the loop can perform; the promise of a nonexistent knob could mislead future
  readers.
- **Thread 9** — the unfenced near-miss detector keyed on a bare `task-ledger`
  heading + `- requirement:` bullets, which is also exactly what a model
  *documenting the format* emits; the silent strip could mangle a correct
  answer. Note the review's example (`status: pass|fixed|fail`) parses
  tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check alone would not close the
  window — the fix requires real verification content instead.
- **Thread 10** — `_stripAssistantLedger` returned after the first
  ledger-bearing block, so a second ledger-bearing text block stayed in the
  transcript, violating the per-message "transcript never shows it" guarantee.
- **Machine-notice threads** (verdict records + `rework-consume` audits,
  `threadId: null`) are audit boilerplate whose own text says "Do not edit or
  reply" — no reply targets. The two review-summary comments (REQUEST_CHANGES
  round + APPROVE round) are answered by this response: the APPROVE leg's one
  remaining IMPORTANT issue is thread 7, fixed below; its three polish items
  are threads 8/9/10, also fixed.

## Approach

TDD per thread — a failing test reproducing the exact scenario first, then the
minimum fix:

1. **Terminal fold (thread 7)** — `_terminalRunMessages` now takes the context
   messages, the strip stash, and the gate flag, and runs
   `_emitFinalizeGateFold` before the early return. Effects: the hidden
   `task_ledger` record persists on error/aborted runs; `AgentEndEvent` ships
   the stripped terminal message (fold rewrites `newMessages` before the
   snapshot), so the in-memory payload and the session JSONL agree; gh-1412's
   "run must end on the answer" is untouched (the fold still only fires when
   the terminal message's original is in the stash).
2. **Comment truth (thread 8)** — the gate-key comment now states that the key
   is read per event from the live config so interceptor and fold agree, and
   that within a run the value is constant because nothing mutates
   `finalizeGate` mid-run. The closure stays (both halves must read the same
   config instance).
3. **Unfenced evidence bar (thread 9)** — new `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` in
   `finalize_gate.dart`, consulted for unfenced spans only (fenced contract
   shape unchanged): two-plus entries, OR a single entry with a non-empty
   `command`/`expected`/`actual`. A lone `- requirement:` bullet — or a status
   placeholder — never classifies a prose section as a ledger.
4. **Per-message strip (thread 10)** — `_stripAssistantLedger` now walks all
   text blocks and replaces every ledger-bearing one, recording ONE stash
   entry per message whose `ledger` stays the LAST block's resolution
   (`ledger ??=` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412 "last block decides"
   event semantics preserved, fold stash-matching untouched.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `_terminalRunMessages` signature +
  pre-return fold; gate-key comment rewritten (thread 7 + 8).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart` — `_stripAssistantLedger`

{"content":"# Fixed — the terminal fold now runs on the error/aborted early-return path

`_terminalRunMessages` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`) now receives the strip
stash, the context messages, and the gate flag, and runs
`_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, currentMessages, strippedLedgers, emit)`
**before** emitting `TurnEndEvent`/`AgentEndEvent` and returning early:

```dart
if (finalizeGate) {
  await _emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, contextMessages, stash, emit);
}
await emit(TurnEndEvent(message: message, toolResults: const []));
await emit(AgentEndEvent(List.unmodifiable(newMessages)));
```

Effects on the failed/aborted path:

- The hidden `task_ledger` record **persists** — the self-check of exactly the
  near-miss case the gate exists to capture is no longer discarded.
- `AgentEndEvent` now ships the **stripped** terminal message (the fold
  rewrites `newMessages` before the snapshot is taken), so the in-memory
  payload and the persisted JSONL agree.
- gh-1412's "run must end on the answer" is preserved: the fold still only
  fires when the terminal assistant message's original is in the stash.

Regression test per your requirement in
`test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`: *"an error/aborted terminal answer
still folds — the hidden record persists and the end payload ships the
stripped message"* — `stopReason: error` + a tool turn + parseable terminal
ledger ⇒ exactly one `TaskLedgerEvent`, and the `AgentEndEvent` payload
contains no `task-ledger`/fence. RED before the fix (zero events), green
after; the surrounding finalize-gate suites stay green.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_7_terminal_fold.md"}

{"content":"# Fixed — comment now states the constant truth

The comment in `_runAgentLoop` no longer promises a mid-run flip that cannot
happen. It now reads:

> The gate key is read per event from the loop's live config so the
> interceptor and the fold always agree on the same value; within a run it
> is constant — nothing in the loop mutates `finalizeGate` mid-run.

That matches the mechanics you traced: `_applyTurnUpdate` only ever replaces
`model` (`copyWith` carries `finalizeGate` through), and a host mutating
`Agent.finalizeGate` post-boot never reaches the loop's config snapshot. The
closure stays (the fold and the interceptor must read the same config
instance per event), but the text no longer implies an honored interactive
toggle.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_8_comment.md"}

{"content":"# Fixed — the unfenced shape now requires real verification evidence

New `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` gate in `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`
(consulted from `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` for unfenced spans only; the
fenced contract shape is untouched):

- **two-plus entries** → accepted (a real near-miss checklist);
- **a single entry** → accepted only when it carries actual verification
  content: a non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual` field;
- otherwise the span is skipped — a prose section quoting the format is never
  classified as a ledger.

A `status` claim alone is deliberately not evidence: your doc example's
`status: pass|fixed|fail` parses tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check
would not have closed the window — but it never carries a
command/expectation/actual, so it is rejected now. A lone
`- requirement:` bullet in particular is never enough.

Regression tests in `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart`:

- *"a model DOCUMENTING the ledger format is not stripped"* — your exact
  heading + single-bullet + `status: pass|fixed|fail` example ⇒
  `parseTaskLedger` null and `stripTaskLedger` byte-identical. RED before
  the fix (parsed as a one-item ledger).
- *"a single-entry near-miss with a real command still parses"* — positive
  control so the tightening doesn't lose genuine one-item self-checks.

All pre-existing unfenced fixtures (two-item near-miss, bold heading, loop
test) carry real commands and stay green.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_9_unfenced_doc.md"}

{"content":"# Fixed — every ledger-bearing block is stripped; the gate key stays last-block

`_stripAssistantLedger` (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart`) no
longer returns after the first ledger-bearing block. It now walks all text
blocks last-to-first, replaces **every** ledger-bearing one, and records ONE
stash entry per message:

- the stash entry's `stripped` message has all ledger blocks removed, so the
  persisted JSONL and the rendered transcript can never show a leftover
  block ("the transcript never shows it" now holds per message, not per
  first-hit);
- the stash entry's `ledger` stays the **last** ledger-bearing block's
  resolution (`ledger ??= ...` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412's
  "last block decides" event semantics are unchanged, so the gate key and
  the fold's stash-matching behave exactly as before;
- one stash entry per message keeps the fold's `identical(entry.original,
  terminal)` matching untouched.

Regression test in `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`: *"EVERY
ledger-bearing text block is stripped — a second block never survives in the
transcript (the gate key stays the last ledger)"* — a message with two text
blocks that each carry a fenced ledger ⇒ both blocks gone from the
`AgentEndEvent` payload, and the single `TaskLedgerEvent` carries the LAST
block's ledger (`revised item`). RED before the fix (the draft block
survived), green after.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_10_multi_block.md"}

{"content":"# 🔧 Rework Complete — gh-1516

All four open review threads on head `6bff6972b` addressed in code, each with a
RED-before/GREEN-after regression test. No open threads were skipped.

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 7 (IMPORTANT)** — error/aborted terminal runs stripped the ledger from
  the persisted JSONL (the `MessageEndEvent` interceptor fires during the run)
  but never emitted the `task_ledger` record: `_terminalRunMessages` returned
  early, bypassing `_emitFinalizeGateFold`. The self-check of a failed
  unattended run — precisely the near-miss the gate exists to capture — was
  silently discarded, and `AgentEndEvent` shipped the unstripped original,
  disagreeing with the persisted session.
- **Thread 8** — the gate-key comment promised a "mid-run flip" that nothing in
  the loop can perform; the promise of a nonexistent knob could mislead future
  readers.
- **Thread 9** — the unfenced near-miss detector keyed on a bare `task-ledger`
  heading + `- requirement:` bullets, which is also exactly what a model
  *documenting the format* emits; the silent strip could mangle a correct
  answer. Note the review's example (`status: pass|fixed|fail`) parses
  tolerant-status as `pass`, so a status check alone would not close the
  window — the fix requires real verification content instead.
- **Thread 10** — `_stripAssistantLedger` returned after the first
  ledger-bearing block, so a second ledger-bearing text block stayed in the
  transcript, violating the per-message "transcript never shows it" guarantee.
- **Machine-notice threads** (verdict records + `rework-consume` audits,
  `threadId: null`) are audit boilerplate whose own text says "Do not edit or
  reply" — no reply targets. The two review-summary comments (REQUEST_CHANGES
  round + APPROVE round) are answered by this response: the APPROVE leg's one
  remaining IMPORTANT issue is thread 7, fixed below; its three polish items
  are threads 8/9/10, also fixed.

## Approach

TDD per thread — a failing test reproducing the exact scenario first, then the
minimum fix:

1. **Terminal fold (thread 7)** — `_terminalRunMessages` now takes the context
   messages, the strip stash, and the gate flag, and runs
   `_emitFinalizeGateFold` before the early return. Effects: the hidden
   `task_ledger` record persists on error/aborted runs; `AgentEndEvent` ships
   the stripped terminal message (fold rewrites `newMessages` before the
   snapshot), so the in-memory payload and the session JSONL agree; gh-1412's
   "run must end on the answer" is untouched (the fold still only fires when
   the terminal message's original is in the stash).
2. **Comment truth (thread 8)** — the gate-key comment now states that the key
   is read per event from the live config so interceptor and fold agree, and
   that within a run the value is constant because nothing mutates
   `finalizeGate` mid-run. The closure stays (both halves must read the same
   config instance).
3. **Unfenced evidence bar (thread 9)** — new `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` in
   `finalize_gate.dart`, consulted for unfenced spans only (fenced contract
   shape unchanged): two-plus entries, OR a single entry with a non-empty
   `command`/`expected`/`actual`. A lone `- requirement:` bullet — or a status
   placeholder — never classifies a prose section as a ledger.
4. **Per-message strip (thread 10)** — `_stripAssistantLedger` now walks all
   text blocks and replaces every ledger-bearing one, recording ONE stash
   entry per message whose `ledger` stays the LAST block's resolution
   (`ledger ??=` on the first reverse hit) — gh-1412 "last block decides"
   event semantics preserved, fold stash-matching untouched.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `_terminalRunMessages` signature +
  pre-return fold; gate-key comment rewritten (thread 7 + 8).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop_finalize_gate.dart` — `_stripAssistantLedger`
  strips all ledger-bearing blocks, one stash entry per message (thread 10).
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — `_LedgerSpan.isUnfenced` +
  `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` evidence gate in `_lastParseableLedgerSpan`
  (thread 9).
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — RED→GREEN: error-stopReason
  terminal fold test; two-block strip test; `textTurn`/`assistant` gained a
  `stopReason` parameter.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — RED→GREEN: documenting-the-format
  rejected (parse null, strip byte-identical); single-entry-with-command
  positive control.

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproduced first**: all three new tests failed on the pre-fix head —
  zero `TaskLedgerEvent` on the error path; the draft ledger block survived
  the strip; the format-documentation answer parsed as a ledger.
- **GREEN after the fix**: finalize-gate suites all pass —
  `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart`, `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart`,
  `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart` (50 tests), plus
  `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart --tags integration` (2/2).
- **Full suite** (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,llm,pty,browser-ext,io,perf`):
  see final count below — no regressions.
- `dart analyze lib/src/cli lib/src/agent test/agent test/cli`: no
  errors/warnings (only pre-existing info-level `unnecessary_import` notices
  in untouched files).
- `dart format` clean on all touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- **CRAP ratchet** (CI's exact tool, `crap4dart 0.11.0`): `analyze` —
  `_terminalRunMessages` CC 4, `_stripAssistantLedger` CC 6,
  `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` CC 5, `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` CC 4,
  `_runAgentLoop` CC 9; Max CRAP 0.00 — OK (threshold 12.00).
  `check --baseline`: 3 passed, 1 warned (the pre-existing warning-severity
  duplication triage debt — unchanged from the previous round).

`_parseLedgerItems` on body:
- `- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>` → entry, requirement = '<verbatim requirement quote>'
- `  status: pass|fixed|fail` → field line, status = 'pass|fixed|fail' → fromName → token 'pass|fixed|fail'.split(whitespace).first = 'pass|fixed|fail', startsWith('pass') → TaskLedgerItemStatus.pass!

So `only.status != fail` → true → looks like a ledger. The placeholder "pass|fixed|fail" parses as pass. Hmm.

The reviewer said: "require at least one entry with a real `status`/`command` field". A "real" status field means a status value that's actually one of the enum values, not the literal placeholder. So I should distinguish "status field present with a recognized value" — fromName is tolerant though. Better: check whether the item's status field actually parses to a recognized token. Options:

1. Check the raw body for a status field with a clean token. But `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger` receives items only.

2. Change the acceptance rule: for a single entry, require non-empty command/expected/actual OR status recognized — where "recognized" means the status token (trimmed) is exactly 'pass', 'fixed', or 'fail' (case-insensitive) or starts with them? But 'pass|fixed|fail' starts with 'pass'...

Hmm. The doc example's status is 'pass|fixed|fail'. What distinguishes a real near-miss single entry from this doc? Honestly the cleanest discriminator per the reviewer: "two-plus entries". 'pass|fixed|fail' — word boundary: 'pass' followed by '|' — `\b` between 's' and '|' is a boundary (word char → non-word char). So `pass|fixed|fail` matches `^pass\b`. Hmm.

Only the fenced shape is used in the CLI/integration tests; the unfenced shape appears in `finalize_gate_test.dart` and `finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` only. Both of those unfenced fixtures carry `command:` (and status pass).

Now decide the rule. The reviewer's example doc:

```markdown
## task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

The cleanest discriminator that keeps all existing positive fixtures green: a single unfenced entry must carry a **non-empty `command`, `expected`, or `actual`** — i.e., evidence of actual verification, which a format quote never has. Status alone (which is the claim, not evidence) is insufficient. Drop the `status != fail` clause.

But wait — what about a genuine one-item near-miss that only has `- requirement: X` + `status: pass` (no command)? It would now be rejected (no strip, no record). That's a deliberate trade-off the reviewer explicitly proposed ("so a single `- requirement:` bullet isn't enough to classify a prose section as a ledger"); and the gate's value is verification telemetry — an item with no verification content is weak anyway. A two-entry unfenced ledger still fires.

Update `_unfencedLooksLikeLedger`:

```dart
bool _unfencedLooksLikeLedger(List<TaskLedgerItem> items) {
  if (items.length >= 2) return true;
  final only = items.single;
  return only.command.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.expected.trim().isNotEmpty ||
      only.actual.trim().isNotEmpty;
}
```

And doc comment: "two-plus entries, or an entry carrying actual verification content (a command or an observed expectation/actual)". A status claim alone is not evidence — it is also the shape of a format quote.

Only the fenced shape appears in CLI/integration tests, so tightening is safe. The discriminator: a `status` claim alone is exactly what a format quote carries — real verification evidence is a `command`/`expected`/`actual` field. Updating the rule:
